verdict.line: You lose if Darius lands E (Apprehend) into a level 2-3 all-in before you have W (Infernal Chains) up to poke from range; you win from level 6 onward by kiting his stackless approach and out-dueling with E (Umbral Dash) knockup and R (World Ender) sustain.

brief.thesis: Darius has zero gap-closer that moves him to you — his only engage is E (Apprehend), a skillshot pull he has to land — while your W (Infernal Chains) out-ranges that pull and roots on hit. Whoever controls that range gap wins lane: if you poke from max W range and never eat a clean E, Darius cannot generate Hemorrhage stacks or Q (Decimate) healing, and he falls off hard once you out-scale him with items and R.

theirWindow.when: He lands E (Apprehend) or gets level 2 first
theirWindow.what: The moment he pulls you in, he chains W (Crippling Strike) into auto into Q (Decimate) for the heal — this is his all-in and it's strongest at level 2-3 before your W is maxed. Trade back immediately with passive (Deathbringer Stance) empowered auto and E (Umbral Dash) second cast to knock him up and buy space rather than standing in the bleed.

yourWindow.when: His E (Apprehend) whiffs or is down
yourWindow.what: Land W (Infernal Chains) at max range for the root, walk in for Q1-Q2 (The Darkin Blade) sweeps, and hold Q3's knockup for if he tries to flash out or re-engage. He has no tool to close distance again until E resets.

start.why: Sustain through Hemorrhage bleed chip damage while you wait for W (Infernal Chains) to hit level 5 for max range poke

boots.why: Darius's damage is entirely physical (autos, Q edge, passive bleed) — steelcaps cut both his all-in and his passive tick

core.why: Proc heal and bonus damage on your first crit-tagged hit rewards landing W root into Q1, and the healing offsets his bleed in extended trades
Shred armor stacks up fast through Q's multi-hit sweeps and lets you eventually out-trade his tanky Crippling Strike build
The shield and tenacity directly counter his W (Crippling Strike) slow and stop him from finishing you off after a Q (Decimate) trade

situational.when: you're ahead and want to no-sell his bleed damage over time in prolonged skirmishes
their team adds burst or AP threats that can finish you off during a Darius trade
you're the primary target of dives and need to punish a bad all-in for free
darius rushes crit items and his autos start one-shotting you post-6

runes.keystoneWhy: Extended trades are where you win this lane once W lands — Conqueror's adaptive damage and melee healing reward you for staying in range instead of one burst window

summoners.why: Teleport lets you reset waves after poke exchanges and keeps you relevant to sidelanes once you start out-scaling him; Flash covers you if you misjudge E (Apprehend) range

playing.title: Poke from max W range only
playing.detail: Land W (Infernal Chains) at the edge of its range and follow with Q1-Q2 rather than walking up first — this keeps you outside his E (Apprehend) hook until the root lands.

playing.title: Save E's second cast to punish his engage
playing.detail: E (Umbral Dash) recast knocks up on hit — hold it to interrupt his all-in the moment he pulls you with E (Apprehend), instead of using both charges just to reposition.

playing.title: Track Hemorrhage stacks in extended fights
playing.detail: At 5 stacks his R (Noxian Guillotine) deals true damage scaled off missing health and resets on kill. Disengage before a long trade lets him stack to 5, especially once you're under 40% HP.

playing.title: Bait Q (Decimate) before committing
playing.detail: His Q heals him only if it hits a champion. If you see him swing it into air or minions, that's several seconds of no sustain — that's your window to walk up and trade.

playing.title: Pre-cast passive before trades
playing.detail: Deathbringer Stance's empowered auto is your biggest single hit — activate it before he lands W (Crippling Strike) on you, since the slow will otherwise deny you landing it.

playing.title: Don't fight him with your R down if he still has his
playing.detail: World Ender's heal-per-takedown is what wins the late trade; if he's got R (Noxian Guillotine) up and you don't, disengage rather than gambling on an even fight.

brief.patchCaveat: Ability names, numbers, and item availability (Sundered Sky, Black Cleaver, Sterak's Gage) reflect the general Aatrox/Darius kit and mid-2020s item system as I know it — verify current numbers, keystone tuning, and whether these exact items are still live before locking the build in champ select.
